title: Pass@k Is Not a Property of a Model: Prompt Format, Decoding, and Statistical Power in Evaluations of RL for Reasoning
content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards is widely reported to raise a base model's reliability (pass@1) while leaving its coverage (pass@k at large k) flat or worse, so that RL sharpens within a reachable set it does not expand. That comparison is read off a sampling surface indexed by prompt format, decoding temperature and scorer, and the standard protocol fixes all three once for both arms in the name of fairness. On one GRPO-trained Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B the choice is not neutral, and neither are three further choices no protocol reports. Giving each arm its own best prompt format, selected out of sample, cuts the measured pass@1 gain on MATH-500 from +36.50 to +12.27 percentage points; selecting on coverage rather than reliability gives +28.03 from the same surfaces; and a transfer claim reads as 6% or 68% depending only on whether it is sized in points or as a ratio. At large k we find a null replicated across three seeds and two benchmarks - and show MATH-500 could not have detected a difference in either direction: 88% of its problems are immovable. Under the exact conditional test coverage comparisons require, the most-cited such comparison could not have reached significance whatever the data did, and our own two are decided at the edge. None of the four had been tested at all. Taking the tuple view constructively, we ask whether a pass@k budget should be spread across cells rather than spent in one, and answer it exactly offline. It should not: RL equalises the decoding cells rather than making them complementary, and does so on a faster clock than coverage - at pass@128 four fifths of the flattening completes before coverage moves at all, though at pass@8 the two move together. Three seeds unioned appear to buy +9.56 pp of coverage while three resamples of a single seed buy +9.12 pp, so union-style gains reported without such a null are largely unreadable. We release the sampling surfaces so that any pass@k protocol can be recomputed without GPUs.
